expected:
# BUG-HOSTMACRO — {HOST.HOST} does not resolve in LLD/item-prototype preprocessing scripts

Discovered while running A2b, not planned as its own scenario upfront — written as its own
expected/actual pair per ground rule 2 as soon as the anomaly was noticed and before the
confirming re-test below was run.

Expected (once suspected): if {HOST.HOST} truly doesn't resolve inside these preprocessing
scripts' string literals, then the canonicalPeerId() sysname-fallback branch
(`'s:' + reporterHost + ':' + local_if_index + ':' + sysname`) degrades to using the literal
text `{HOST.HOST}` for EVERY reporter, identically. Two different reporters, each with a
chassis-less neighbor sharing the same local_if_index and the same remote_sysname, would then
collapse into ONE node instead of two — a direct violation of §4.1's explicit requirement that
the s: form "must never become a global sysname match."
actual: Confirmed directly: two different reporters (TM-Collide-A, TM-Collide-B), each reporting a DIFFERENT chassis-less neighbor sharing local_if_index=1 and remote_sysname='Collision', both produce the identical tag topo.peer.id='s:{HOST.HOST}:1:Collision' -- the literal macro text, unresolved. The assembler therefore renders ONE 'Collision' node instead of two. Root cause: Zabbix does not expand {HOST.HOST} inside this discovery rule's/item prototype's JavaScript preprocessing string literals (at least not the way it's written here, inside a quoted JS string assigned to a var) -- it was ASSUMED to work by analogy with other preprocessing contexts (documented as a 'deliberate substitution' in CTopologyTModel.php's own doc comment) and this assumption was never verified live until this campaign. This directly breaks the §4.1 guarantee that the sysname fallback 'must never become a global sysname match' -- it currently IS a global sysname match (scoped only by local_if_index, not by reporter at all).
proposed_uc_verdict: A2's 🟡 does not go far enough for the sysname-only case: as currently implemented this is a 🔴 (silent false-merge across unrelated reporters), not just a missed-merge inconvenience.
notes: NOT fixed as part of this campaign per ground rule 1 (do not modify the implementation while testing it). Likely fix: resolve the reporter's own hostid/host via a JSONPath-style lookup against a value already available to the script (e.g. pass it through as part of the blob itself, since push.py already knows its own zabbix_host name) rather than relying on {HOST.HOST} macro substitution inside Duktape-executed JS, OR confirm via Zabbix documentation/source exactly which macros ARE substituted in LLD-rule vs. item-prototype preprocessing scripts before retrying.
